 CHA @ ATL | IND @ CLE | ORL @ BKN | TOR @ DET | NOP @ OKC | WAS @ CHI | PHX @ UTA | HOU @ DEN | SAC @ LAL 
 Charlotte Hornets at Atlanta Hawks 
 Team Totals: Hornets 107, Hawks 112.5 
 Injury Report: Hornets: Grayson Allen (O, concussion), Kon Knueppel (O, hamstring), Dennis Schröder (O, hamstring), Grant Williams (O, hamstring). Hawks: Mouhamed Gueye (O, foot), Jock Landale (O, toe), C.J. McCollum (O, calf), Asa Newell (O, toe), Henri Veesaar (O, ACL), Kingston Flemings (Q, back) 
 Hornets projected starters: Coby White, Brandon Miller, Sion James, Naz Reid, Moussa Diabaté 
 Hawks projected starters: Kingston Flemings, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson, Onyeka Okongwu 
 Lee quotes: Said the guys late in the LAL game hit their minutes limit and they didn’t want to push them past it, said “they have a big picture in mind” with keeping the minutes down, said it was uncharacteristic for them to get beat on the O boards, said they were switching/blitzing on Luka and it worked out, said Naz will be evaluated for his injury late vs. the Lakers. 
 Snyder quotes: Said “we need to run, pass the ball, break the paint, play defense” to win games, said Dyson Daniels ’ impact is never reflected in the box score, said Kispert stayed ready and even blocked a shot, said Dort and Wiggins “were really focused” in their return to OKC. 
 Stats and Notes: 
 *The Hornets should’ve won against the Lakers, and their minutes-restriction issues just keep popping up. That’s not going to change any time soon, so it adds prolonged capped ceilings on guys. Charlotte is still sitting at the second-slowest offensive pace, and they’re the worst offense in the NBA. The only reason to go there today is that the Hawks at least play at the fastest O pace in the NBA. The Hawks are getting killed at the basket, but the Hornets have a horrendous interior offense. They have the highest 3Pr in the NBA and some of the worst interior scoring. Nope. On the other side, Atlanta leads the NBA in transition offense, and the Hornets are average there. The Hornets also have been getting killed on jumpers, and it should set up pretty well for the ATL perimeter guys. Plus, the Hornets have been getting destroyed on drives, moving to a 53.7 FG% on drives for one of the worst marks in the NBA (they don’t allow a lot of drives, though).  As usual, the Hornets are rebounding well. 
 * Brandon Miller will see a heavy dose of Dyson Daniels , and it’s not exactly an ideal spot. He’s not driving, and a whopping 73.9% of his shots are coming via jumper. At least he played 32 minutes last game, so maybe he can do enough with this team lacking creation. He did have a 2-of-14 shooting line against Dyson last time, so yeah. Not great. 
 * Naz Reid ’s matchup is pretty decent with the Hawks being a bad rim defense. It’ll be a good bit of Jalen Johnson guarding him, and Naz isn’t relying on his jumper too much, with 52.1% of his shots coming off those. With so many players having minutes limits, maybe Naz can really put up a big number. 
 *It’s a decent matchup for Moussa Diabate because the Hawks get beat inside a bit, with Atlanta giving up a ton of putback points. Still, there’s just no ceiling here. 
 * Coby White ’s minutes did come up to 26 last game, but man, he’s been awful. His 34.0 eFG% on jumpers ranks third worst in the NBA ( Jalen Johnson , Scoot Henderson ). I hate it (took a lot of Coby in best ball). 
 *It’s a solid spot here for Nickeil Alexander-Walker . He leads the NBA in C&S attempts, with Charlotte giving up a decent bit of those. He will see a decent bit of Sion James , which is totally fine. His role actually didn’t grow too much without C.J. McCollum in the last game, but I’d expect that to shift a bit here. I like him a lot. 
 *In the last game, Jalen Johnson was the team’s leader in touch time and drove it 17 times against an elite OKC defense (guarded by Isaiah Hartenstein a bunch). This matchup is a solid one with Naz Reid likely to guard him (some Sion, too). It will be tough for him to really put up a big number because the rebounding stuff won’t be there.  
 * Dyson Daniels could really rack up the steals against this careless team. It’s not a great matchup on offense, but he could just pile it up off his steals. In fact, Dyson had seven steals in this matchup earlier this year. Don’t sleep on him here. 
 *I’m not into Onyeka Okongwu for rebounding in this spot, and there are some really good center spots on the slate today. 
 Great matchups: Dyson Daniels 
 Good matchups: Jalen Johnson, Moussa Diabate, Naz Reid 
 Bad matchups: Brandon Miller
